workingTitle: 语义码率与共享拥塞控制的耦合稳定域
researchBoundary: Analyze the coupled dynamics created when multiple cooperative-perception senders adapt semantic content or period from marginal perception value while a shared congestion controller adapts the resource limit from channel load.

nearestWorkBoundary.work: ETSI TS 103 324 CPS and TS 103 141 BME
nearestWorkBoundary.occupiedSpace: CPS can choose CPM frequency, object count, and area count for value of information under a BME resource limit; BME updates that limit from channel load.
nearestWorkBoundary.openBoundary: The BME policy is outside the standard scope and no coupled semantic-controller stability result is specified.

nearestWorkBoundary.occupiedSpace: A shared A-DCC-like BME and local value thresholds form part of the same system.
nearestWorkBoundary.openBoundary: CPM period remains fixed, thresholds do not feed back into BME, and the authors explicitly leave BME convergence and threshold-period interaction for future work.

nearestWorkBoundary.occupiedSpace: Discrete congestion-control stability, synchronized updates, linear feedback, and utility-fair convergence without perception-semantic feedback.
Stable resource shares for heterogeneous service demand and priority rather than instantaneous marginal perception value.

noveltyBoundary: Measure the cross-sender coupling produced by shared channel load and redundant semantic utility rather than treating every sender controller independently.
Derive and validate a gain, delay, update-period, and node-count stability boundary.
Define semantic starvation only when a sender retains positive marginal utility but receives persistently negligible normalized service.
Separate protocol-level stability from any later claim about neural perception quality.

publicStack.name: Artery, Vanetza, OMNeT++, and SUMO
verifiedEntrypoints: src/artery/envmod/service/CpService.cc implements CPM generation and object-utility ordering with DCC period constraints.
cmake --build build --target run_example is the documented smoke entry.
publicStack.executionBoundary: Source and documentation were inspected, but this audit did not compile the stack.

twoWeekMinimum: Compile the pinned Artery environment and reproduce an official example before adding the candidate controller.
Create 2, 5, 10, and 15 sender scenarios and log per-node CPM size, period, channel-busy ratio, queue, and send and receive events.
Implement a bounded local update from marginal semantic utility and congestion error with configurable feedback delay and minimum service.
Sweep synchronized and asynchronous updates, 50 to 500 ms control periods, 0 to 500 ms feedback delay, load steps, and heterogeneous value profiles.
Report paired stability maps, trajectories, Jain fairness, starvation duration, and controller-component ablations.

preregisteredOperationalDefinitions.persistentOscillation: During the final 20 seconds, peak-to-peak rate exceeds 20 percent of the usable range and does not decay.
preregisteredOperationalDefinitions.semanticStarvation: A sender with positive marginal utility remains below 10 percent of its normalized fair share for five continuous seconds.

baselines: Quality over Quantity-style fixed-period threshold control
sixWeekStudy: Freeze one OpenCOOD or OPV2V model and export payload size and receiver marginal task utility over compression and object-threshold settings.
Replay those utility and payload traces through the completed Artery controller matrix instead of coupling live neural inference.
Estimate the equilibrium Jacobian spectral radius and compare the predicted boundary with observed oscillation and starvation.
Use multiple seeds and report a stable null envelope when no instability is found.
falsifiableClaims: Semantic and congestion feedback produce a measurable off-diagonal utility coupling between senders.
A gain-delay-node-count boundary predicts persistent oscillation better than network load alone.
A minimum-service or passivity-inspired stabilizer reduces semantic starvation without hiding congestion in another queue.
When semantic feedback is disabled, any remaining oscillation is classified as a network-control or numeric effect.
killCriteria: The pinned Artery example cannot be reproduced in three working days.
No cross-sender marginal utility derivative is measurable after freezing other senders.
Oscillation persists with semantic control disabled.
The observed boundary changes with simulation step size and fails a finer-step check.
The OpenCOOD checkpoint cannot be reproduced by week three; remove perception-quality claims and retain only the protocol study.
implementationRisks: The direct Quality over Quantity implementation is unavailable.
Receiver marginal semantic utility and redundant-information accounting require a frozen definition.
The primary Artery path is ITS-G5 and cannot be generalized to C-V2X sidelink without a separate transport replication.
OpenCOOD's older environment and storage requirements can dominate the six-week schedule.
